subject.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles

question: Is the process-local retired-row ledger plus fresh-key retry strategy acceptable for this P1 fix under the documented best-effort hard-restart announce boundary?
rationale: The implementation and proof support normal operation and graceful restart, but only an owner can accept the residual hard-crash context loss and possible overlapping retry turns as the permanent lifecycle tradeoff.

options.title: Accept the bounded tradeoff
options.body: Merge after refreshing the branch, treating hard-restart announce loss as the existing documented limitation and tracking durable exactly-once recovery separately if needed.

options.title: Require durable recovery first
options.body: Hold merge until wave membership, child findings, and retry identity are stored in canonical SQLite state with forced-restart and ambiguous-timeout regressions.

options.title: Pause this wake design
options.body: Close or redesign the PR if maintainers do not want an additional synthesis turn and retry mechanism in the requester lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded tradeoff
recommendation.body: Merge after refreshing the branch, treating hard-restart announce loss as the existing documented limitation and tracking durable exactly-once recovery separately if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent descendant-settle wake and are the clearest feature-history owner for deciding whether the top-level extension preserves that lifecycle contract.
